args.summary: checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the v2.3.1 deploy, with error rate spiking to 18%. Rolled back all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Rollback verified: service healthy again in all regions with error rate at 0.2%. v2.3.1 needs investigation before any re-deploy.
args.title: checkout-api health check failures after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
All done. Summary:

1. **Diagnosed**: v2.3.1 (the latest deploy) was unhealthy in all production regions with an 18% error rate.
2. **Rolled back**: All regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) rolled back to **v2.3.0**, the most recent release that was healthy in production.
3. **Verified**: checkout-api is healthy again across all regions, error rate down to 0.2%.
4. **Incident opened**: **INC-0001** (SEV2) — on-call engineer has been paged, with a full description of the failure and the rollback action taken. v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the root cause is investigated.

transcript.content: I'll first check the deployment history to find the most recent healthy release.
The current production version v2.3.1 is unhealthy across all regions (18% error rate). The most recent release that was healthy in production is **v2.3.0**. Rolling back now:
transcript.reasoning_content: The most recent healthy release in production is v2.3.0. Roll back to it. Rollback doesn't require approval per policy (only deploying never-healthy versions). Then create SEV2 incident. Rollback and incident — incident describes what I did, so ideally after rollback completes. They're arguably dependent (incident describes rollback result). I'll do rollback first, then incident.

transcript.content: Rollback verified — service is healthy again in all regions (error rate back to 0.2%). Now opening the SEV2 incident:
